newsitem.title: UK: Global investors overweight marks - Merrill survey.
newsitem.headline: Global investors overweight marks - Merrill survey.

text.p: Global investor portfolios shifted from a net underweight to a net overweight position in German marks, Dutch guilders and Swiss francs in the three months to August, according to the latest survey of international fund managers by U.S. investment house Merrill Lynch.

The quarterly survey showed that Merrill's net exposure index, compiled from the returns of 73 institutional fund managers from the U.S., Europe and Japan, rose to 55.0 in August for marks, guilders and Swiss francs from 44.0 in May.
An index reading of 50.0 is considered neutral.

The exposure index to the non-mark European Union core currencies -- defined by the French franc, Belgians franc, Danish crown and European currency unit -- showed investors still underweight but it was up slightly during the three months to 35.0 from 33.5.

A sharp decline in exposure, however was registered in the bloc defined by the European high-yielders -- the Italian lire, Spanish pesetas and Swedish crowns. The index for this group fell from an overweight position of 52.0 in May to 42.0 in August.

"It appears that each time investors shifted their allocations between the mark and the high-yielding European currencies they exposed themselves to an eventual market reversal," said Merrill's head of research Michael Rosenberg, in a text accompanying the survey.
"Indeed, a contrarian would probably move at this juncture to go long the core and high-yielding bond markets and their currencies and short the German bond market and the mark."

Net exposure to the dollar, meantime, remained overweight but dropped 6.5 points to 60.25 during the three months to its lowest level since May 1995. It was the biggest quarterly decline in dollar exposure since early 1993.
